title: A Franklin Society reissue
summary: George Simon is putting together a Sauter-Finegan reissue.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: By the way, we probably should get on tape, if you wish, what you mentioned about George Simon calling you this morning and saying they are interested in putting out a recording of some of the Sauter-Finegan material. Do you want to describe that?
More than that I don't know. He simply informed me of what is happening, he's putting the thing together for the Franklin Society. Beyond that I really don't know.
Is there any kind of a chance that you know of that more of that material would be put out, and how would you like to see it reissued? Do you have any ideas about that?
At this point I don't care. If I have any concern (inaudible).

Other than bread and butter I don't care about it. If it provides me with shelter and food and clothing, and increasingly, drugs for health reasons, because I'm getting older; if I don't have to go begging for that sort of thing that's fine. If that could in any way provide me with the necessities, then it's important to me; otherwise, it's not.
